They're friendly. They're not on your side.

Insurance companies profit when you take less. The adjuster's job is to close your Van Nuys claim cheap, fast, and quiet. It's not personal. It's the business model.

  • They'll ask for a recorded statement while you're still on pain medication. Every word gets used.
  • They'll offer a check before anyone knows whether you need an MRI. It's sized for someone without a lawyer.
  • If you wait to see a doctor, they'll call it proof you weren't hurt.
  • They'll pin part of the blame on you to trim the number. California lets them try. You don't have to accept their percentage.

You shouldn't have to learn their playbook while your body is trying to heal. That's what you hire us for — and it costs you nothing until we win.

The recorded statement

The treatment gap

Shared fault

California lets you recover even if you were partly at fault. Don't sign their version.

Waiting is the most expensive thing you can do.

California generally gives you two years from the crash to sue. If the crash involves the city, the county, or a transit agency, you may have only six months to file a government claim. Miss it and the case can die no matter how badly you were hurt.

The clock that actually kills cases is faster than the law:

  • Store and freeway cameras overwrite in days
  • Witnesses stop answering
  • The other driver “remembers” a different story after talking to their insurer
  • You wait to see a doctor, and they call that a gap

Call now. If there's no case, we'll tell you straight — no fee, no pressure. If there is, the letters to preserve the video go out today.

What everyone asks

What does it cost?
Nothing up front. Nothing out of pocket. We front the case costs and take a fee only if we win. If we don't win, you don't pay a fee.
They already offered me a check.
Don't cash it yet. That first number is what they pay people who don't have a lawyer. Send it to us — free — and we'll tell you in plain terms whether it's fair. It almost never is.
I was partly at fault.
You can still recover. California reduces your payout by your share of fault — it doesn't erase it. The adjuster's percentage is an opening bid, not a verdict.
Will I have to go to court?
Most cases settle. We prepare every case like it won't, because that's what moves the number. If they won't pay what it's worth, we go.
I don't have papers / I didn't go to the ER / I don't speak English.
Call anyway. Your immigration status does not affect your right to recover in California. If you skipped the ER, there's still a case — waiting longer is the only thing that makes it worse. And you don't need English. Ismael is on the team.
